newsitem.title: USA: Dennis Trading tops 1996 CTA returns at 111.41 pct.
newsitem.headline: Dennis Trading tops 1996 CTA returns at 111.41 pct.

text.p: Dennis Trading Group, run by fund manager Richard Dennis, topped the returns of Commodity Trading Advisors (CTAs) and hedge funds for 1996 with a return of 111.41 percent, according to fund monitor TASS Management Ltd.
Richard Dennis, along with his partner William Eckhardt, in the 1980's popularized a systematic trading approach known as the Turtle System, based on following long term trends.
William Eckhardt's CTA trading program was also one of the top performers in 1996 with a return of 46.75 percent, TASS Management noted.

"In 1996 we continued to see a trend of systematically oriented CTA's posting the top returns, with energy, currency and foreign bond markets providing the best trading opportunities," Tass Management chief executive Nicola Meaden said.

For the month of December, currency-oriented programs which stressed strategies such as going long the US dollar were top peformers, and for the year trades based on being long Britsh pounds and short Swiss francs and Japanese yen were profitable.
The British pound saw a 48 month high against the US dollar, the Swiss franc saw a 30 month low against the dollar, and the yen saw a 45 month low against the dollar in late 1996.
Trades in crude oil and natural gas markets were also notable winners in 1996, TASS said.
Crude oil saw five year highs in 1996, while natural gas prices saw all time highs.
The so-called European convergence trade on European interest rates was also a popular strategy, TASS said.
"While December was generally not strong for CTAs, 1996 was one of the best years of the decade for the CTA community, with September, October and November being good months," Meaden said.
In December, nine of the top ten funds in the TASS rankings were systematic traders, while for the year, eight of the top programs were fully systematic, TASS said.
The monthly "TASS Flash Report" follows the performance of 68 CTA programs, each with a minimum of $45 million under management.
TASS Management Inc is a London-based research company which tracks the performance of about 1,600 "alternative investment" managers and funds globally with $9 billion under management.
"Alternative investments" include hedge funds, CTA programs, managed currency managers, emerging market funds and funds of funds.
